messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: page fired -> high 5xx error rate on /v1/generate (threshold: 10% over 5m) :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Incident INC-2024-1115 created, urgent, assigned to on-call: ron (oncall)
oncall note: please ack within 2m to avoid escalation
ron (oncall): acked. pulling up dashboards now.
maya (SRE): seeing ~15% 5xx across region-us-west over last 3m. spike started ~3:12 UTC.
alex (runtime): adding logs from gateway:
```
[2024-06-03T03:12:05Z] runtime-gateway-prod-3 -> upstream runtime: 502 Bad Gateway, upstream read timeout
[2024-06-03T03:12:06Z] kv-cache-miss for prefix tokenized:user:abc123
[2024-06-03T03:12:07Z] model-runner-12 oom; restarted (killed by OOMKiller)
```
ron (oncall): OOMs on model-runner-12... any recent rollout?
sophie (eng): we rolled v2.3.4 to 20% canary ~3:05 UTC targeting larger context lengths. could be memory regression.
maya (SRE): corroborating — p95 mem per instance rose ~22% after rollout. request QPS steady. error type is backend 5xx not client rate limits.
pagerduty: Escalation: unacked by additional responder in 3m -> paging maya (SRE)
maya (SRE): I'm on. temp mitigation plan: 1) quiesce canary (stop traffic to v2.3.4), 2) scale up model-runner pool + restart unhealthy pods, 3) monitor error rate.
alex (runtime): prepared redwoodctl commands:
```
# move traffic off canary slice
redwoodctl route update my-model --variant v2.3.4 --weight 0
# scale runner pool
redwoodctl pool scale model-runner --replicas 24
```
ron (oncall): executing route update now.
incident-bot: Command executed by ron (oncall): `redwoodctl route update my-model --variant v2.3.4 --weight 0`
sophie (eng): can we also set fallback to v2.3.3 for safety?
alex (runtime): doing fallback toggle: `redwoodctl route update my-model --variant v2.3.3 --weight 100`
incident-bot: Command executed by alex (runtime): `redwoodctl route update my-model --variant v2.3.3 --weight 100`
maya (SRE): scaling runners and restarting crashed pods (k8s restarts in progress).
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart sts/model-runner
kubectl get pods -l app=model-runner -w
```
ron (oncall): PD ack shows maya and alex acknowledged. incident severity: SEV2 (customer-facing increased error rate).
15m check-in: customers impacted primarily via host region-us-west; high-traffic tenants saw transient failed requests (est. 2% of all requests retried by clients).
maya (SRE): metrics update: error-rate dropped from 15% -> 1.8% within 120s after traffic cut and restarts. latency stable.
sophie (eng): good. any errors tied to quantization path or new attention kernel?
alex (runtime): root cause hypothesis: v2.3.4 increases memory per-request under long-context; on saturated nodes this led to OOMs and upstream 502s. not a kernel correctness issue.
ron (oncall): posting customer comms draft to #support: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors for the /v1/generate endpoint between 03:12–03:16 UTC affecting some requests. Traffic was routed away from the canary and service restored. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." any suggested edits?
sophie (eng): add: "no PII exposed, no data loss" and mention rollback to v2.3.3.
ron (oncall): added and sent. support acked.
maya (SRE): creating incident ticket and runbook tasks: postmortem, memory regression test for v2.3.4, canary sizing guidance, and automated canary abort gate for memory p95.
```
# incident artifacts
- incident ticket: INC-2024-1115
- timeline + logs attached to ticket
- runbook task created: RB-824
```
alex (runtime): keeping v2.3.4 frozen in staging. we will run memory-profile jobs against a synthetic long-context load.
maya (SRE): handing off monitoring and follow-ups to ron for the next shift. ron, you own the postmortem + customer follow-up thread.
ron (oncall): taking handoff. leaving notes: 1) rollback complete, 2) error rates stable <0.5% for 10m, 3) next steps for eng: memory diff, canary abort gate, stress tests.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-1115 status -> mitigated; paging stopped; assigned to ron (oncall) for post-incident follow-up. :white_check_mark:
maya (SRE): thanks all. we should add a pre-deploy memory regression check to CI for large-context models.
sophie (eng): agreed. will spin up action item in planning board.
ron (oncall): closing the realtime page thread. follow-up will be in INC-2024-1115 doc and scheduled postmortem meeting.
incident-bot: Thread closed at 2024-06-03T03:28:20Z
